title: Gate induced strain on a two-dimensional hole gas in silicon
authors: D. van der Bovenkamp, C. S. A. Müller, B. D. Pantiru, I. Bošnjak, M. Cignoni, Q. Torrent Nicolau, M. E. Bal, S. Wiedmann, J. Ridderbos, F. A. Zwanenburg
abstract: We show the effect of gate-induced strain on the valence band of a silicon (Si) metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) confined two-dimensional hole gas (2DHG). Increasing aluminum gate thickness, and thereby the strain in the channel, results in the onset of a second subband contributing to Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations. Temperature-dependent magnetotransport measurements reveal distinct cyclotron masses of $m_c^*=(0.36\pm0.04)m_0$ and $m_c^*=(0.49\pm0.02)m_0$. The measured cyclotron masses differ from those expected for an idealized heavy-hole (HH)/light-hole (LH) picture, reflecting the combined influence of quantum confinement, strain, and HH-LH mixing on the valence band.
summary: This work demonstrates that strain induced by an aluminum gate can locally modify the valence band structure of a silicon two-dimensional hole gas. By analyzing Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations, the authors extract multiple cyclotron masses, proving that confinement and strain together dictate the electronic properties. This establishes a powerful method for engineering quantum material behavior using standard semiconductor fabrication techniques.
main_problem: To investigate how strain, locally induced by an aluminum gate, modifies the valence band structure of a two-dimensional hole gas (2DHG) in silicon.
main_result: The measured cyclotron masses deviate from simple heavy-hole/light-hole predictions, confirming that quantum confinement and strain combine to significantly alter the valence band structure. The technique allows for local engineering of electronic properties using standard semiconductor fabrication methods.
method: The study combines transport measurements (Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations) analyzed via temperature dependence fitting (Lifshitz-Kosevich theory) with theoretical simulations (COMSOL finite-element solver) to model strain effects.
model_or_system: The physical system is a 2DHG confined at the Si/SiO2 interface. The valence band structure is modeled using concepts like HH-LH mixing and incorporating strain tensors ($\epsilon_b$, $\epsilon_{rot}$) into the Hamiltonian formalism (Bir-Pikus context).
key_observables: Cyclotron masses ($m_c^* \approx 0.36 m_0$ and $0.49 m_0$), Shubnikov-de Haas oscillation frequencies/amplitudes, and simulated strain components ($\epsilon_b$).
important_parameters: Gate thickness (20–100 nm) acts as the tuning parameter for strain magnitude; cryogenic temperatures ($T \approx 1.3$ K); magnetic field ($B = 9$ T).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting SdH oscillations using the Lifshitz-Kosevich factor, and initial modeling assumes a framework incorporating confinement and strain effects beyond simple bulk approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $\Deltaho_{xx}$ vs $1/B$ and FFT amplitude vs frequency, showing how gate thickness controls the appearance of multiple oscillation peaks ($f_2$). Simulations map out the spatial variation of biaxial strain ($\epsilon_b$) near the gates.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform (Si 2DHG) and the tool (gate-induced strain). It presents transport measurements showing evidence of multiple subbands via SdH oscillations. Theoretical analysis confirms that simulated strains are sufficient to modify band structure on the meV scale, linking theory to experiment.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the ability to use external fields/geometry (gate voltage/thickness) to tune fundamental electronic band structures in solid-state systems is highly relevant for designing quantum devices and controlling spin-orbit coupling effects.
